Caption / description / post text:
POV: your favorite Taco Bell item never actually left…you just didn’t know how to make it at home yet 👀🌯 I'm a former Taco Bell employee, I’m showing you exactly how to recreate the Quesarito (well, about as close as you can realistically get) The secret is the creamy chipotle sauce 🔥 Chipotle Sauce: 1 cup mayo 2 whole chipotle peppers in adobo ½ tsp adobo sauce (from the can) ½ tsp chili powder ½ tsp sugar ½ tsp salt ¼ tsp garlic powder ¼ tsp onion powder ¼ tsp paprika (smoked is ideal, but regular works as well) Blend until smooth.  Use right away or chill to let the flavors develop. What you need: • Burrito-size tortilla • Taco-size tortilla • Nacho cheese (Fritos jalapeño cheddar is closest IMO) • Seasoned rice (microwavable precooked works great) • Taco meat (simmer in water + seasoning for softer texture) • Shredded cheddar • Sour cream How to make it: Warm the large tortilla, spread nacho cheese + shredded cheddar, then place the smaller tortilla on top. Add rice, taco meat, chipotle sauce, and sour cream. Wrap it up, then toast in a dry skillet on both sides until lightly browned. And just like that, you’ve got a homemade Quesarito 🌯🔥 I’ve already done the enchirito, beefy 5 layer, crunchwrap, cheesy gordita crunch, 7 layer, and chicken quesadilla…what should I recreate next? 👇 #quesarito #tacobellathome #tacobellrecipes #budgetmeals #realisticcooking #copycatrecipe

Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
I'm a former Taco Bell employee and I'm showing you how to recreate your favorite Taco Bell menu items at home. Today we are making the very requested quesarito. Before we can make the burrito though, first we have to make the sauce. The quesarito features their creamy chipotle sauce, which also comes on the grilled cheese burrito, the spicy potato taco, and their cantina items. To make it add 1 cup of mayonnaise to a blender, along with 2 whole chipotle peppers, and a small spoonful of adobo sauce, both from one of these little cans, along with the seasoning mix I have listed below. Blend that until it's creamy and this one is ready to use right away, or you can chill it in the fridge to let those flavors marinate. Once you've got that, here's what else you'll need. Tortillas, you will need a burrito size and a taco size tortilla. Nacho cheese. I get a ton of questions about this, I've tried almost every store bought nacho cheese I've also tried several homemade recipes. Over the years I have settled on the Fritos jalapeno cheddar. It's not perfect, but to me it's about as close as you're going to get. Seasoned rice. One of these little packets of pre-cooked Spanish rice will work just fine. If you want to make it from scratch, by all means, but I'm doing my best to make these as easy, affordable, and convenient as possible. Taco meat. Just go with your favorite. If you're aiming for ultra tender meat, simmer the meat directly in the water and seasoning without browning it first. Lastly you'll need shredded cheddar cheese and sour cream. Warm up the burrito size tortilla first, add on a spoonful of nacho cheese and some shredded cheddar. Then add on the taco size tortilla, a scoop of rice, a scoop of taco meat, some of that homemade chipotle sauce, and some sour cream. Wrap it up, then toast it in a dry skillet on both sides until it's lightly browned. And you have just made the Taco Bell quesadillo at home, or as close as you realistically can. In just a recap so far I have shared the Enchirrito, the beefy five layer burrito, the Crunchwrap Supreme, the cheesy gordita crunch, the seven layer burrito, and the chicken quesadilla. If anyone is looking for those, please check out my Taco Bell at home playlist and let me know what you want to see me recreate next.
